$comment: Each task is a NATURAL-LANGUAGE request, graded on three separate things so a
tools_ok     — were the tools that answer this actually called? (`expect_tools`)
args_ok      — did the tool's own RESULT carry the expected value?
answer_ok    — did the model's final answer, in prose, state the same value?
Every expected value in `assertions` was produced by running the shipped tool
(see benchmark/_probe.mjs), never typed from memory: a benchmark whose ground
truth is recalled rather than measured grades the author, not the model.
`expect_absent` is a restraint check — a tool that must NOT be called, because
the request is answerable without it or the request is not a bioinformatics
Regexes are matched against whitespace-collapsed text. Numbers are written
loosely (e.g. `[0-9.]+`) ONLY where the tool itself rounds; the rounding is
then pinned by the matching `where: "tool"` assertion, which reads the exact

tasks.instruction: My digest of pUC118.dna (working directory) with BamHI is barely working — almost no cut, even though the site is definitely in the sequence. Someone suggested Dam methylation. Work out what is going on: check the plasmid's Dam and Dcm sites, and tell me what the methylation analysis says about BamHI and which enzymes the tool considers usable on this plasmid.

assertions.note: the tool flags BamHI

the methylation verdict must be reported. NOTE what is deliberately NOT asserted here: there is no assertion that the model AGREES with the tool. Measured behaviour is that it runs molbio_methylation_check, then cross-checks NEB over the web, finds the plugin's reference table disagrees (the table marks BamHI impaired by dam; NEB lists BamHI as dam-insensitive), and reports the disagreement. That is the right thing to do with a quick-reference table, so this task grades whether the model CONSULTED the analysis, and the table discrepancy is recorded in benchmark/README.md as a plugin-data question instead of being scored as a model failure.

tasks.instruction: Here are my qPCR Ct values from a knockdown experiment. Target gene: treated 22.1, 22.3, 22.0; control 25.0, 25.2, 24.9. Reference gene: treated 18.0, 18.1, 18.0; control 18.2, 18.1, 18.3. What is the fold change in the target gene in the treated samples relative to control, by the delta-delta Ct method?

assertions.note: fold change, rounded however the model likes

assertions.pattern: mismatch @seq1 (31|81) / seq2 (31|81): (A vs C|C vs A)
assertions.note: exactly one difference, at read position 31 and reference position 81. The assertion is deliberately AGNOSTIC about which argument is which: the resolver passed `sequence1 = read`, and `molbio_align` reports identity symmetrically, so pinning `seq1 81 / seq2 31` graded an incidental argument order rather than the alignment. Both orderings and both base polarities are accepted; what is NOT accepted is a missing or additional difference.

tasks.instruction:
Translate this DNA in frame 1 and find the open reading frames of at least 5 amino acids. Tell me the protein sequence and the length of the longest ORF in amino acids.

GGGATGGCTGCTGCTGCTGCTGCTGCTGCTGCTTAACCC
Explain the difference between how BsaI and EcoRI cut DNA: their recognition sites, how many bases away they cut, and what kind of overhang each leaves.

assertions.pattern: BsaI: type IIS GGTCTC\(1/5\), cut 7/5, 4 bp 5' overhang

assertions.note: EcoRI's site. Matched WITHOUT its leading G on purpose: the model legitimately writes the cut notation `G^AATTC` (and the spaced `G^A A T T C`), neither of which contains the contiguous literal `GAATTC`. Pinning the exact literal graded the model's typography rather than its answer — the first version of this assertion failed a fully correct response for that reason.
both enzymes leave a 4 nt overhang

tasks.instruction: I am running an EcoRI+HindIII double digest of pUC118.dna (full length 3162 bp, in your working directory) on a 1 kb ladder gel. Draw me the expected band pattern, and tell me how many bands I should see and whether the small fragment will be visible.

assertions.note: the backbone fragment. Accepted as either the exact size or its conventional `~3.1 kb` shorthand: both are correct answers to this question, and demanding the digits graded how the model chose to round rather than whether it got the digest right.
the small fragment's exact size — this one IS pinned, because it is the number that explains the whole answer

assertions.pattern: 1 band|one band|2 band|two band|1 fragment|2 fragment|single .{0,12}band
assertions.note: the band count. The model is EXPECTED to distinguish the two theoretical fragments from the single band a 1 kb-ladder gel actually resolves, so both counts are accepted.

assertions.pattern: not visible|too small|will not|won't|below|faint|run off|dye front|below detection
assertions.note: a 51 bp fragment is not resolvable next to a 1 kb ladder

tasks.instruction: No bioinformatics needed for this one, I just want to sanity-check my arithmetic: if I dilute 10 microlitres of a 50 mM solution into a final volume of 500 microlitres, what is the final concentration in mM?

assertions.note: 10 uL x 50 mM / 500 uL = 1 mM

tasks.instruction: Can you check my sequencing result for me?

assertions.note: the missing input must be asked for
the model must say it has nothing to work with rather than guess

a clarification, not a one-line refusal: at least 500 characters of substance. The first version demanded a literal `?`, which failed a perfectly clear bulleted request for the missing files — the headless composition has no question answerer, so the model is told to ask in prose and does so without question marks.
